text:
The person wants the pet feeder to put less food in the dog's bowl tonight.
give rex less fod tonight pls
Half a scoop for Rex this evening
Could you cut down his dinner a little?
Rex ate too much yesterday, so make his bowl smaller
Don't fill the bowl all the way
He made a mess on the carpet, so please add only a small amount of food tonight
I'd like a lighter dinner for the dog
Would you mind asking the feeder to hold back a bit? The vet told us he is a little heavy and we should go easy.

name: loud_storm_warning
does: Tells you if thunder or loud storms are coming to a place on a certain day.
inputs: a place and a day
people say:
- Will it be loud outside on Wednesday?
- Is thunder coming this week?
- Should I replace the picnic with a movie night, or will the sky stay calm?
- Any storms near Leeds tomorrow?
- Do I need to bring the dog in before it gets rough out there?

Mara got home from the hospital at seven in the morning. She was so tired that her eyes kept closing. Yesterday she had told her son she would put up the holiday lights, and she hated the thought of lying awake worrying about it. She sat down on the couch and said to the smart speaker, 'Tree lights, please.' The speaker understood that she meant the plug for the lights on the Christmas tree in the front room. It turned the plug on and said the tree lights were on. Mara smiled. Then she asked it to turn them off at ten at night and on again at six each evening. The assistant set up that plan and said it out loud so she knew. Mara closed her eyes, and the glow of the tree stayed with her as she fell asleep.

Finding a film to watch is easy when you let an assistant help. You say what kind of movie you want, and it shows a short list. It might be a dog movie for the kids, a scary one for Friday, or something short for a train ride home. People change the list by saying things like show me only new ones, nothing too long, or skip the sad ones. If the first choice looks weak, you can say try again or give me another. You can also ask for a trailer before you decide, or for the times at the cinema near you. To change the time, you just say later tonight or what about Saturday.

When something at home breaks, an assistant can help you fix it or book someone who can. A leak in the attic, a noisy fan, or a dirty filter at the bottom of the heater can all be handled the same way. You say what is wrong and when you are free, and the assistant finds a repairer. People change the plan with short words. They say move it to Friday, make it the morning, or cancel that one. If the visit has to go earlier, they ask if someone can come sooner. For small jobs, the assistant can remind you to change a filter every three months. When the repairer is on the way, it tells you, so you know when to go to the door.

name: plant_light_check
does: Compares how much sun two spots in a garden get and says which one is better for a plant.
inputs: the name of a plant and two places in the garden
people say:
- Where should my basil go, the porch or the back fence?
- Which spot gets more sun for tomatoes?
- I grow herbs for pasta and need a bright corner.
- Compare the sunny bed with the shady one.
- Are my round pots too dark by the wall?

Walter was not good with phones, but his daughter had put a voice assistant on the kitchen table. One morning he looked in the mirror and sighed. His hair was so long it was touching his collar, and he did not want to miss the wedding on Saturday. He said, 'My hair is getting in my eyes, and the big day is very close.' The assistant understood that he needed a haircut. It asked which shop, and he said Tony's, the one he always used. It found a free time on Thursday at ten and booked it. Then it told him, 'Your haircut at Tony's is on Thursday at ten.' Walter's wife asked it to find a tailor to fix her skirt too, and it read out the shop hours.

Lena ran a small shop that sold jam and honey. Her best customer, Mr. Boyd, had a birthday coming, and she wanted to welcome him with a little gift. She asked her phone, 'What do I give a man who has everything? Find something that costs half of what I paid last year.' The assistant understood that she wanted gift ideas at about half of last year's price, which was forty dollars. It said an average gift in that range is a tin of tea or a small plant, and it listed three ideas. Lena picked the tea. Then she asked for a reminder two days before the birthday, and the assistant set it and said the reminder was saved.

Weather forecasts tell you what the sky will do, so you can plan your day. Many people think of them as just rain or sun, but they also show the heat, the wind and the chance of rain. If you are on a tight budget and want to walk instead of taking the bus, you might check whether an empty field will turn to mud. You can ask for a different place, a different day, or just the next hour. People say what about tomorrow, how cold will it be tonight, or will it rain at five. If you want less detail, you say just the short version. If you want more, you say tell me about the whole week.

The person wants to know how many days are left until a date.
How many days until June first? No wait, I meant July first.
days left till the deadline
Count the days to my sister's wedding
I'm sitting in my cozy chair planning the year, so could you tell me how long until the report is due?
Is it a lot of days until Christmas?
How long till my birthday?
Wait, not the first, I meant the fifteenth
Tell me how many sleeps until the trip

Omar drove a delivery van, and by the time he got home he only wanted to sit down. The washer was running in the back room, and his daughter was watching cartoons on a tablet downstairs. He said to the TV, 'Connect to the sports channel, but not the news. I don't want the news tonight.' The assistant understood that he wanted the football game and no news. It switched the living room TV to the sports channel and said the game was starting in ten minutes. It also asked if he wanted subtitles, and he said no. The assistant left them off and kept the volume the same. Omar put his feet up and waited for the game.

name: find_old_email
does: Searches your inbox for an old message by who sent it or what it was about.
inputs: a name or a few words from the message
people say:
- Where is that email from my aunt about the party?
- I had a dozen messages from the school, show me the last one.
- My head hurt when I read that note about the bill, find it again.
- Dig up the sad letter my friend sent me in May.
- Show me anything from Tom this week.
- Find the message with the train ticket.

name: bin_day_reminder
does: Tells you which bin to put out and on what day.
inputs: your street and the kind of bin
people say:
- Which bin goes out tomorrow?
- The man from the council said it changed, so when do they come now?
- Remind me the night before green bin day.
- Do the bright blue bags go out on Monday?
- Did I miss the pickup? I saw the truck fly by.

Knitting is a hobby many people enjoy in the evening. You use wool and two needles to make a scarf or a hat. A cat on your lap can make it harder, so keep the wool in a safe basket. When you make something, you decide on the color, the size and how soft it should be. People say make it longer, use thicker wool, or try a bigger needle. A helper can also count your rows so you do not lose your place. You can say how many rows have I done, or start again from row ten. And to remember what to make next, you can say put a hat on my list.

name: coffee_strength_setter
does: Sets how strong, how big and how hot the coffee maker makes a cup.
inputs: the strength, the size of the cup and the heat
people say:
- Make it stronger, I need fuel for the day.
- Not so bitter, please.
- Give me the exact same cup as yesterday.
- I want a slow drip coffee, medium size.
- Weaker for my mum, coffee makes her jumpy.
- Hot, but not boiling.

A packing list helps you remember what to take on a camping trip. You need a tent, a sleeping bag, water and food. Small things matter too, like a torch and a lighter. There is no microwave in the hills, so people take a small stove. A list can change every day, depending on the weather and how long you stay. People say add a rain jacket, delete the heavy boots, or move the stove to the top. The assistant can check the daily forecast for the hills and tell you if the nights will be cold. When you are done, you can say this is the list for the lake, so you can find it again next year.

Measurements tell us how big, how heavy or how hot something is. A recipe may ask for grams, but your scale shows ounces, so people ask for the other kind. They say how many cups is that, how many pounds are in a kilogram, or what is twenty degrees in Fahrenheit. The current temperature outside may be in one kind of degrees, and your friend far away uses another. Before you pack a bag for a trip, you might check the weight limit. A weather map may say a cloud is six kilometers high, and you might ask how many miles that is. People change a number by saying use the other unit, or give it in feet instead.

The person wants the wifi to work faster and stop dropping.
Wifi is slow
Fix the internet, please
The video keeps freezing, can you clear it up?
Why is my connection so bad tonight?
Make the internet smooth again
Can you restart the router for me?
We can't load anything and I think the router is stuck
Excuse me, my niece has an online swim class in five minutes and the picture keeps stopping, so could you please make the wifi stable again? She would be very grateful.

Rosa locked up her shop late on Friday and noticed the camera light was off. She had been reading an article on her phone about break-ins, and that made her worry. She typed fast, with no capital letters: turn on the back door camra and message me if it sees anything. The assistant understood that she wanted the camera at the back door switched on, with a message sent to her phone if it saw movement. It turned the camera on and said so. Rosa picked up her bag and walked home, knowing the shop would be watched all night.

name: clip_trimmer
does: Cuts a short video so only the part you want is left.
inputs: the video, where to start and where to stop
people say:
- Cut the first ten seconds off my video.
- Remove the dirty bit at the end where I dropped the phone.
- Keep only a fraction of it, just the last half minute.
- Make this clip shorter so I can send it.
- I only want the part where she blows out the candles.

name: free_time_finder
does: Looks through your calendar and finds a time when you have nothing planned.
inputs: a day or a week, and how long you need
people say:
- When am I free on Thursday?
- Find me an hour this week to pick up milk and run errands.
- Look at my calendar and tell me when I'm not busy.
- I need to be ready for a meeting, is there a gap before lunch?
- Is the afternoon open?
- Any space for a long call tomorrow?

Grandpa Joe had a letter to send, but his knees were bad and the post office was a long walk. He sat by the window with his tablet and said, 'My knees are too sore for the walk to the post office, and I can't hand in this page myself.' The assistant understood that he needed someone to deliver his letter. It found a pickup service that collected mail from homes and asked if he wanted a driver that afternoon. Joe said yes. The assistant booked a pickup for three o'clock and told him the cost. At three, a woman in a shiny red van knocked, took the page in its envelope, and drove off. Joe never had to leave his chair.

Priya had ten minutes before she had to leave, and she was still trying to dress. Her phone was on the bed, and she had no free hand. She typed with one thumb: call mom on spekaer. The assistant understood that she wanted to call her mother with the speakerphone on, so she did not need to tap the screen again. It dialed, and Mom's voice filled the room. It was the final call before the trip, and Priya asked about the bus time while she pulled on her shoes. When the call ended, the assistant said so. Priya grabbed her keys and ran out the door.

Mrs. Alvarez, a retired teacher, liked to read a bedtime story to her granddaughter on the phone every night. Tonight she also had a doctor's visit to think about, and she had to report to the clinic at eight in the morning. She said to the smart speaker, 'Excuse me, would you please wake me at six thirty tomorrow, because I have to be at the clinic by eight and the bus takes an hour?' The assistant understood that she wanted an alarm at six thirty and set it. It repeated the time to her. Then a sudden noise from the kitchen made her jump, and she asked for a ten minute timer to watch the kettle. The assistant started it.

Sam was already in the car when he remembered the garage was open. He was far from the house, and the neighbor's boy was coming to mow the lawn at noon. He said into his phone, 'Is the front door locked, and who rang the doorbell?' The assistant understood that he wanted the lock status and the doorbell history. It said the front door was locked, the garage door was open, and the doorbell had rung once, twenty minutes ago, when a courier left a box. Sam asked it to close the garage, and it did. It also showed a clip of twenty-five seconds from the camera, so he could see the box on the step.

Dee woke up on moving day with a headache. The kitchen was a mess, and the last project was packing the dishes. She mumbled, 'I need more boxes, double what I have, and what do I do with the cooked rice?' The assistant understood two things. She wanted to order boxes, twice the ten she already had, and she needed a tip for the leftovers. It ordered ten more boxes for same day delivery and said cooked rice keeps for a day in the fridge, so she could pack it in a small cooler. It also reminded her that her brother, who wanted to design the layout of the new living room, was coming at two.

Nina was a busy parent, and her phone had buzzed twenty-five times since breakfast. She stood outside the school with her toddler on her hip and said, 'Turn off post alerts for two hours, I'm going for a jog after drop off. And change my profile picture to the one from the beach.' The assistant understood two things. She wanted her social media notifications muted for two hours, and she wanted the beach photo as her new picture. It did both and told her the alerts would come back at eleven. Nina smiled, put the phone in her pocket and pushed the stroller toward the park.

Kofi came home after a night shift in November, when the mornings were still dark. She wanted to rest, but first she wanted to put away the video of her niece's school play. She said to her tablet, 'Move my school play video to the family folder, and make it half as long. There is too much extra at the start.' The assistant understood that she wanted the clip saved in the family folder and cut down to half its length, with the first part removed. It moved the video, trimmed it, and said the new clip was two minutes long. Kofi pressed play, smiled at her niece in a paper crown, and went to bed.

Ivan had a small shop a kilometer from the station. Late in the day he saw a strange email saying his shop account had a new login. He typed fast on his phone, with no capital letters: cancle the shop login on the black laptop and change my password. The assistant looked at the list of devices, found one called Black Laptop, and signed it out. Then it asked him to say a new password, and he picked a long one. The assistant saved it and told him that the old password no longer worked. Ivan locked the shop, feeling a lot safer.

Smart lights let you change a room with your voice. A lamp can be bright when you read and soft when you want to chill. You can also change the color, like a warm yellow for dinner or a cool blue for work. People say make it dimmer, a bit brighter, or turn off the ceiling light. If you want a mood, you can say something cozy for movie night. Someone hosting a spicy food night might ask for a warm red glow. Someone reading by the window with the old bridge in view might ask for the lamp to be a little brighter. The lights simply do what the words say.

Tao was a student with an exam in the morning. He lay down on the rug in his room, but he saw that he had left his alarm unset. There were only six hours left until the exam. He had to dig his phone out from under a pile of notes. Then he said, 'Alarm, six sharp.' The assistant understood that he wanted an alarm at six in the morning and set it. It told him, 'Alarm set for six.' Tao also said, 'Sleep sounds.' The assistant started soft rain sounds and said it would stop them after an hour. Tao closed his eyes and soon he was asleep.

Grandma Ruth was moving to an apartment up north to be near her son. Her son was going to fly in on Friday to help her. She picked up the tablet and said, 'I don't want the big truck, and I don't want to pay for packing. Find me a small mover. What is the number of the one I looked at last week?' The assistant understood that she wanted a small moving service that did not pack her things. It found the company from last week, read out the phone number slowly, and offered to call it for her. Ruth said yes, and the assistant dialed. A friendly man answered on the second ring.

Mr. Haddad, a retired teacher, planned to visit his sister by the sea. He sat at the table with a slice of toast and asked his phone, 'Find me a hotel with a small room, no more than half of what I paid last time. And I want a thick curtain, because I sleep late.' The assistant understood that he wanted a hotel room for two nights at half the price of his last stay, which was two hundred dollars, so about one hundred. It added the curtain to the search. It found three places and read them out. Mr. Haddad picked the second one and asked the assistant to keep it for him.

name: return_item_helper
does: Starts a return for something you bought and gives you a label to print.
inputs: the order and the reason
people say:
- This bread arrived stale, send it back.
- I want to return the cat bed, it's too small.
- Point me to the returns page for my last order.
- The bag is the wrong size, can I swap it?
- Get my money back for the shoes.

Person: Hello. Would you please read me the headlines? I am stuck in a long meeting and I hope to catch up before lunch.
Assistant: Sure. Which kind do you want, local news, sports or world news?
Person: Sports, please. I'm a little bored of the same stories.
Assistant: Here are two sports headlines. The city team won at home last night, and a runner broke a record at the weekend.
Person: Great. Can you tell me who will win tomorrow's game? I'll think about it on my walk to the station.
Assistant: Sorry, I can't know that. I can tell you when the game starts, if you like.

name: voice_note_saver
does: Records what you say out loud and saves it as a note.
inputs: your voice and a name for the note
people say:
- Write this down: call the neighbor about the fence.
- Jot down the idea I had in the middle of the night.
- Remember that I need to check the oven filter.
- Keep what I'm about to say.
- Save a note for the shopping trip.

Ben drove a taxi, and at the end of the day he pulled onto his street and saw a tree branch lying next to the bins. A bird began to tweet in the tree above him. He said to his phone, 'What goes in the green bin, and is this branch okay?' The assistant understood that he was asking about garden waste. It said the green bin takes branches shorter than twenty-five centimeters, and bigger ones need a special pickup. There was not enough room in the bin for the long branch, so Ben asked the assistant to book a pickup. It did, and told him the day.

Grandpa Lou always spoke very politely, even to machines. He took his morning dose of pills with tea and then said to the garden speaker, 'Excuse me, if it isn't too much trouble, could you please start the robot mower at nine tomorrow? My grandson is visiting, and I want the lawn done before the heat of the afternoon, because the grass is too long for his ball.' The assistant understood that he wanted the mower to start at nine in the morning. It set the plan and said so. The next day the little red mower rolled out right on time, and Lou watched from his chair, pleased.

Camila was a cook in a busy restaurant, and she had a note about the dentist stuck to her fridge. One morning she said to her phone, 'Excuse me, could you please book me a dentist visit on Tuesday after lunch? My back tooth hurts and I would like to go before the weekend rush at the restaurant.' The assistant understood that she wanted a dentist booked on Tuesday afternoon. Cars zoom past the window of the office. A soft voice at the dentist answered the call, and the assistant found a time at two thirty. It booked it and added it to her calendar.

The person wants to know what an amount costs in another currency.
Euros to dollars?
How much is that in dollars?
What's fifty pounds in yen?
Tell me the rate for pesos today
The shelf sensor says twenty euros, what's that in my money?
I'm creating a budget for my trip, so what is a hundred euros in Swiss francs?
Show me today's rate, it never stays constant
What would this cost me back home?

Hana drove a bus, and when she got home the house was cold. She said to the thermostat, 'Make the living room two degrees warmer, and just the radiator by the window.' The assistant understood that she wanted two more degrees in the living room, with only the window radiator. It tried, but the thermostat was offline, so it told her plainly that it could not change it yet and suggested checking the wifi. While she waited, Hana went to tidy the hall. She found the back window open by an inch and shut it. A minute later the thermostat came back, and the assistant raised the heat.

Jay was a teenager watching his baby sister while Mom was out. He ate an apple and texted the assistant: no loud alarms, just text me if the baby monitor hears crying. Snow was falling outside, and a sudden gust shook the window. The assistant understood that he wanted no sound alarm, only a text message on his phone when the monitor heard crying. It turned the sound alerts off and the text alerts on. It said, 'No loud alarms. I will text you if she cries.' Jay put the phone on the arm of the couch and watched the snow.

Translating words helps when you travel or talk to a neighbor who speaks another language. You say a word or a phrase, and the assistant says it back in the other language. At a cafe abroad, you may ask how to say one soda and a sandwich. People change it by saying say it slower, spell it, or use the polite way. A phrase can sound funny when said wrong, so people ask how to say it right. If a translation does not seem right, they say try another word. If a phone call with a friend disconnects while you practice, you can say start again from the last line.

Person: Is it going to rain?
Assistant: Where do you want the forecast for?
Person: Where my dad lives. He's on the coast.
Assistant: I don't know where your dad lives. What town is it?
Person: Hartley. And show me twice as many days, I'd like to see the whole week. Sorry, undo that, just the next two days.
Assistant: Okay, two days for Hartley. It will rain tomorrow morning and be dry after lunch.
Person: Good. Should I leave the window open for the cat?
Assistant: I'd close it before the morning.

Tess was a cook, and her hands were wet from washing pots in the sink. She said to the kitchen speaker, 'Turn the music down by half. The walls here are thin and the neighbors go to bed early. And record a note: buy more flour.' The assistant understood two things. It lowered the volume to half of what it was and saved a voice note that said buy more flour. It told her, 'Music is at half. Your note is saved.' Tess dried her hands and went back to the dishes, humming softly.

Person: Put on the show, please. I'm making tea.
Assistant: Which show? I see a few you watch.
Person: The cooking contest. The final one of the season.
Assistant: The final episode of the cooking contest. Which channel do you want?
Person: Channel twenty-five.
Assistant: Okay, it is on channel twenty-five now.
Person: Can you divide the screen so I can see the news too?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't split the screen. I can switch back to the news when the show ends.

Mia was nine, and she was supposed to be in bed by eight, but tonight there was pizza. She sat on a high stool by the window and typed to the speaker, wher is the pizza, its late. The assistant understood that she was asking when the food delivery would come. It looked up the order and said the driver was ten minutes away and was stuck behind a slow truck. It told her the delivery had been paid already, so nobody needed to find money. Mia watched the street until the headlights stopped outside and the doorbell rang.

Person: It's dripping from the ceiling again.
Assistant: Sorry to hear that. Do you want me to book a repair? Which room is it in?
Person: The kitchen, over the stove where I fried the chicken last night.
Assistant: Got it. When would you like the repairer to come?
Person: As soon as possible. Can you display the free times on the screen?
Assistant: Here are three times today. Two o'clock, four o'clock and six o'clock.
Person: Two o'clock.
Assistant: Booked for two o'clock. I'll tell you when the repairer is on the way.

Person: Turn on the fan, please. I've been in the garden all day.
Assistant: Which fan, the one in the bedroom or the one in the hallway?
Person: The hallway. Actually no, the one in the bedroom.
Assistant: Okay, the bedroom fan is on. Low or high?
Person: High. And can you replace the old electric fan in the kitchen with a new one?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't buy or install a fan. I can put one on your shopping list, if you like.
Person: Yes, please do that.

Person: I'm new here. Can you set a timer for my bread and tell me how long the dough should rise?
Assistant: Sure. What kind of dough is it?
Person: Plain white bread, in a warm kitchen. I'm leaving for work soon.
Assistant: It usually rises for about an hour. I'll set a timer for one hour. Do you also want a baking timer?
Person: Yes, please. The oven fan is noisy, so I might not hear it.
Assistant: Then I'll make the alarm loud. Forty minutes for baking?
Person: Thirty. And what jam would pair well with it?
Assistant: Strawberry is a good pair for white bread.
